text: MarkdownAdrSource and adrs_at() must read every .md file in the ADR directory, excluding only the directory's own README, index and template files, as decided by is_record().
quote: read every `.md` file in the ADR directory except the directory's own `README`, `index` and `template`, decided by `is_record()`

text: The source adapter must not filter ADR files by requiring the filename to begin with a digit, which silently skipped names like ADR-001-title.md.
quote: A misnamed file is a lint finding, not a silent gap.

text: parse_adr() must take the ADR number from the title first, recognizing the shapes `# 1. Title`, `# ADR-001: Title`, `# ADR 001 Title`, `# [ADR-001] Title` and `# 001 - Title`.
quote: `parse_adr()` in `src/adrcheck/adapters/markdown_adr.py` takes the number from the title first, in any of the shapes `# 1. Title`, `# ADR-001: Title`, `# ADR 001 Title`, `# [ADR-001] Title` and `# 001 - Title`

text: When the title yields no number, parse_adr() must fall back to the filename via filename_number().
filename_number() must accept a leading number with or without an ADR prefix.
quote: which accepts a leading number with or without an `ADR` prefix

text: filename_number() must treat a leading date (eight digits or yyyy-mm-dd) as not a number, so a date slug never becomes an ADR number such as 20220819.
quote: treats a leading date, eight digits or `yyyy-mm-dd`, as not a number

text: A record with no number from either the title or the filename must be kept with number None rather than dropped, and lint must report it as `missing-number`.
quote: A record with no number from either source is kept with `number` None, and `lint` reports it as `missing-number`

text: Leading zeros must not matter: ADR-001, 0001 and 1 resolve to the same record, and references in text resolve the same way.
quote: Leading zeros do not matter: `ADR-001`, `0001` and `1` are the same record, and references in text resolve the same way.

text: Two files that resolve to the same number must still be reported by lint as `duplicate-number`.
quote: Two files that resolve to one number are still `duplicate-number`.

text: When a title number and a filename number both exist and differ, the title number must win.
quote: a title number wins over a filename number when both exist and differ
